THIS MISCELLANEOUS FIRST APPEAL IS FILED UNDER  SECTION 173(1) OF MV ACT, AGAINST THE JUDGMENT AND AWARD  DATED 25.02.2010 PASSED IN MVC NO.1822/2009 ON THE  PRESIDING OFFICER, FTC AND MEMBER MACT, SAUNDATTI,
 DISMISSING THE PETITION FILED UNDER SECTION 166 OF THE MV  ACT.
 -2-  NC: 2024:KHC-D:749  MFA No. 22844 of 2011  THIS MISCELLANEOUS FIRST APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT Heard Shri. Srinivas Nadamani for Shri.

Jagadish Patil, learned counsel for the appellant and Shri.
S. K. Kayakamath, learned counsel for respondent No.2.
2. Unsuccessful claimant in MVC No.1822/2009 has preferred this appeal.

3. Facts in brief which are necessary for disposal of the present appeal are as under:
3.1.

In respect of road traffic accident said to have been occurred on 23.03.2009 involving motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-24/H-1579, a claim petition came to be filed which was registered in MVC No.1822/2009.
4. The claim petition was resisted by the Insurance Company by filing detail written statement including the date of very accident itself.
5. The Tribunal after raising necessary issues recorded the evidence of the claimant and Dr. Jyoti Prakash M Sultanpur.
15 documents were placed on record on behalf of the claimant.
On behalf of respondent, Sri. Vaiju Chandru Shingyannavar is examined as RW.1 and Ravi Venkatgouda Rangangoudar is examined as RW.2.
On record 24 documents were placed on record on behalf of the respondent.

sentences.text: The Tribunal after taking into consideration both oral and documentary evidence placed on record in a cumulative manner came to be conclusion that there is a delay of five days in lodging the complaint and very date of accident itself is not properly mentioned and doubted the injuries sustained by the claimant in the road traffic accident said to have occurred on 23.03.2009 as is claimed by the claimant and dismissed the claim petition.

7. Being aggrieved by the same, the claimant has preferred the present appeal on the following grounds:
"1. That the Judgment and Award passed by the learned Fast Track Court MACT,
Saundatti, is illegal and arbitrary, since the same has been passed without considering the material documents and evidence on record.

2. It is Submitted that the tribunal error to appreciate the fact that there is doubt about accident occurred and after lapse of 5 days complaint has been filed and come to conclusion that there is a NC: 2024:KHC-D:749 suspicious, only these reasons dismiss the claim petition.
3.
It is submitted that, the tribunal dismiss only on the ground that there was no establish the accident occurred and construct the put forth story.
Therefore, the tribunal error to appreciate the fact on the basis of assumption under the suspicious.

4. It is submitted that the tribunal without considering the EX-P-2 Complaint,
EX-P-3 Spot Panchnama, Ex-P-4 MVI Report, and come to conclusion that complaint deposition of witnesses and photos are different, only these grounds dismiss the claim petition.

5. It is submitted that tribunal has failed to appreciate the fact that the appellant was taking treatment from the date of accident by Dr. M.M.Hooli Hospital treated the appellant from 23/3/2009 to 28/3/2009.
That the tribunal without considering these facts dismiss the claim petition.

6. That the Tribunal erred in dismissing the claim petition without considering the material document Ex.P-5 wound certificate and Ex P-12 X- ray that due to Motor vehicle accident the appellant has sustained grievous injuries but the tribunal failed to observation of the court below, it self is erroneous and unwarranted and ought to have allowed the claim petition filed by the appellant herein.
NC: 2024:KHC-D:749 7.

That on going through the entire judgment it reveals that the tribunal pre determined to dismiss the petition and for that, the tribunal has made only minute contradictions, erred in passing the illegal and erroneous judgment and award.

The tribunal ought to have considered that, it is a summary trial and matter has to be Basavva W/O Basappa Hoolikatti vs Mahabaleshwar Channappa Pattanshetti on 11 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/12498997/

sentences.text: 8. That the tribunal failed to appreciate the full fact this case and not consider proper evidence and case material without considering the true facts and the tribunal dismiss the claim petition.
9. It is submitted that, the tribunal failed to considering the appellants sustained injuries due to the said grievous injuries the tribunal irrespective the fact dismiss the claim petition.

10. That the tribunal without considering the oral and documentary evidence and without discussing each and every aspects of the claim of the petitioner appellant in a proper and perspective manner, passed the impugned erroneous judgment in a hurried manner which is liable to be set aside."
8. Shri. Srinivas Nadamani for Shri.

Jagadish Patil, learned counsel for the appellant vehemently contended that the Tribunal has misguided itself into the material documents placed on record on behalf of the claimant and appreciated the NC: 2024:KHC-D:749 case of the respondent and wrongly dismissed the claim petition resulting the miscarriage of justice and sought for allowing the appeal.

9. Per contra, Shri. S. K. Kayakamath vehemently contended that the very MLC report itself is received on 28.06.2009 and its shows that the MLC report is concocted document and other material evidence placed on record especially in the cross examination of the claimant has been rightly appreciated by the learned Trial Judge and dismissed the claim petition and sought for dismissal of the appeal.
10.

He also pointed out that Ex.P.2 complaint does not disclose the exact date of accident and therefore, there is a doubt as to the road traffic accident said to have been occurred on 23.03.2009 and so also involvement of the motorcycle in question and rejection of the claim petition is thus just and proper and sought for dismissal of the appeal.
11. In view of the rival contentions of the parties, this Court perused the material on record meticulously.

12. On such perusal of material on record, following points would arise for consideration:
NC: 2024:KHC-D:749

i ) Whether the claimant has successfully established that he has sustained injuries mentioned in wound certificate marked at Ex.P.5 in the road traffic accident that has occurred on 23.03.2009 at about 5.00 p.m., involving the motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-24/H-1579?

Basavva W/O Basappa Hoolikatti vs Mahabaleshwar Channappa Pattanshetti on 11 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/12498997/

sentences.text: If so, whether the claimant is entitled for compensation and what is the quantum of compensation?

iii) Whether the impugned judgment is suffers from legal infirmity and perversity and thus call for interference?
iv)
What order?

Points Nos.1 and 3 :
13.
In the case on hand, there is a clear admission on behalf of the claimant that there is a delayed complaint lodged in respect of the accident.
Admittedly the complaint came to be lodged on 28.03.2009 for the accident said to have taken place on 23.03.2009.
The explanation offered by the claimant in this regard is that he has suffered injuries and therefore, he was shifted to hospital and the delay has occurred in lodging the complaint.
14. In respect of the same, the claimant has placed reliance on the Medico Legal Certificate produced at Ex.P.5.
NC: 2024:KHC-D:749 Medico Legal Certificate is no doubt issued on 28.06.2009.

But on close scrutiny of the contents of Ex.P.5, it is crystal clear that the injured has visited the hospital with the history of road traffic accident produced on 23.03.2009 at 5.00 p.m., involving the vehicle and he has been treated in OPD No.271/37 dated 23.03.2009 at about 6.50 p.m.
15.
After registering the complaint marked at Ex.P.2 an FIR came to be lodged as per Ex.P.1.
Charge sheet is marked at Ex.P.6.
At the time of filing the charge sheet the Investigating Officer has collected the Medico Legal Certificate from the hospital.
16. Medico Legal Certificate is no doubt dated 28.06.2009.

Just because the Medico Legal Certificate is dated 28.06.2009 that itself cannot be treated as a doubtful document inasmuch as what is the date that has been contained in Medico Legal Certificate is the certificate issued on 28.06.2009.
Just because it is dated 28.06.2009 which is the issuing date, it cannot be construed that the Ex.P.5 has been concocted for the purpose of case.
17. This aspect of the matter has not been properly appreciated by the learned Trial Judge in the Tribunal.
The fact remains that in Ex.P.2, there is no mention as to when he lodged the complaint.
But the First Information Report discloses that it has been registered on 28.03.2009.
Mere non mentioning of date of the complaint itself cannot be a ground to reject the claim petition.

Basavva W/O Basappa Hoolikatti vs Mahabaleshwar Channappa Pattanshetti on 11 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/12498997/
5 19.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: After the complaint came to be lodged, the police have thoroughly investigated the matter and filed the charge sheet against the rider of the motorcycle.
These aspects of the matter prima facie establish that the claimant has sustained injuries in the road traffic accident.
20. It is settled principles of law that the proof of accident in a matter of this nature need not to the extent of proof in a criminal trial.
21. The claimant is required to place on record the prima facie materials to show that he has sustained injuries in a road traffic accident to lay a claim in a Motor Accident Claims Tribunal.
This aspect of the matter has not been considered by the learned Trial Judge in dismissing the claim petition.
22. Therefore, a case is made out by the claimant for interfering in the impugned judgment and award.

On re-appreciation of material placed on record, this Court is of the considered opinion that the claimant has been successful in establishing that he has sustained injuries mentioned in the wound certificate at Ex.P.5 in the road traffic accident said to have taken place on 23.03.2009.
24.
Accordingly, point Nos.1 and 3 are to be answered in the affirmative.
25. Regarding point No.2: The above discussion now drives this Court to assess the quantum of compensation.

Quantum since needs to be assessed for the first time before this Court, the same is assessed as under:
1 Pain and suffering 50,000/-
2 Loss of amenities 30,000/-
3 Loss of income 1,17,000/-
(5000X12X13X15/100) 4 Medical Expenses 30,314/-
5 Attendant and nourishing charges 2,000/- 6 Loss of income during laid up 15,000/-
 period (3 months)
Total Rs

sentences.text: The injured is aged 50 years as could be seen from Ex.P.5.
He has sustained injuries as is mentioned in Ex.P.5.

In - 11 - NC: 2024:KHC-D:749 the absence of any proper proof of monthly income that has been placed on record for the accidental injuries of the year 2009, monthly income is to be assessed to Rs.5,000/-
for the person aged 50 years and proper multiplier would be 13%.
27.
Suitable amount is to be paid on the heads of pain and suffering, loss of amenities, loss of income during the laid up period and nourishment and attendant charges.

Therefore, the quantum of compensation is assessed as under:
1 Pain and suffering 50,000/-
2 Loss of amenities 30,000/-
3 Loss of income 1,17,000/-
(5000X12X13X15/100) 4

Medical Expenses 30,314/-
5 Attendant and nourishing charges 2,000/- 6 Loss of income during laid up 15,000/-
 period (3 months)
. Accordingly, point No.2 is answered in the affirmative.

29. In view of the above findings of this Court on point Nos.1 to 3, the following order is passed:
- 12 - NC: 2024:KHC-D:749 ORDER
(i) Appeal is allowed.
(ii) Impugned judgment passed in MVC No.1822/2009 dated 25.02.2010 is herby set aside.
